p.b: ACRME — CVAL/DR Shared-Reservation Model (Steady State ↔ DR Event)
p.span: ONE shared reservation pool (100 units) stays fixed — only the CONSUMER subscriptions swap: CVAL (steady state) → DR (disaster)

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
📝 Each grouping still expands into 1 regional + per-AZ CRGs (CAP-023) for zone isolation.
This diagram follows CRG Grouping 2 (CVAL+DR) through its two operating states below.

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
➡️ DR DECLARED → CVAL sacrificed, DR takes over (DR-006 staged sequence)
1️⃣ Shut down / disassociate CVAL VMs → 2️⃣ Free reserved capacity → 3️⃣ Authorize DR consumer subs → 4️⃣ Deploy prod-failover VMs on SAME reservation
🔁 Reversible on failback — DR consumers released, CVAL resumes (DR-013)

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
🧮 Accounting (CAP-015 / FIN-008)
─────────────────────────────
Shared reservation counted ONCE at provider; apportioned by actual consumer allocation.
Steady-state CVAL cost and DR overcommit are the SAME single cost, not duplicated (FIN-008).
Not double-counted as both live CVAL and available DR headroom (HC-6 / HC-7).

div.style: color: rgb(0, 0, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
⚠️ Constraints
─────────────────────────────
📍 Same region + same AZ only (CAP-011 / CAP-013)
📊 Each consumer needs its own quota (QUA-013)
🚫 Prod pool NEVER shares with CVAL/DR (ENV-003)
🔁 Reversible on failback — DR released, CVAL resumes (DR-013)
